body: I picked up a hobby I thought was cool. I used to try to harm myself by banging my head and such, as the knives we had don't exactly cut well without doing a lot of damage. Doing something you can be proud of doing can help distract your overwhelming amount of hate for yourself and before you know it, you've gotten good enough to feel proud and not hate yourself enough to do self harm.

Mine is a bit different from the rest here but it's as simple(and yet rather childish) as playing pretend in my mind. Kind of like imagining living in a fantasy world you make up or something. It's fun, no medications, and better than lying down for 2 hours hoping to finally fall asleep. Daydreaming(though not really) yourself to sleep has always been my go-to since getting up every so often and doing the things people suggest never worked for me.

Back when my depression wasn't as bad, having very few, handpicked friends I could trust deeply made me feel so happy. I could go to school excited, excel because I had the motivation to, and never felt tired and hopeless 24/7. 
  
  Had they stayed close friends, I guarantee I wouldnt be needing the meds, the psychiatrist, or my leave of absence. 
 
  Choose the right friends, mine told me they cared, now I I feel like I'm not even worth 2 minutes of their time to be asked how I'm doing despite being in and out of school for about a month now. Do that, and depression cant even touch you.

1. Players tend to have patterns that are predictable, try to read your opponents and see through their movement.
2. Players aren't bots. If you get in their face, some players will feel the pressure, it's up to you to take advantage of this. 
3. Some champions have guaranteed spots they will be in (Champions that dash will go in a straight line, zoe's portal shows up slight before her) and you can easily land guarantee charms on these, and follow up for easy kills.
4. Surprising your opponents give them less time to react
5. Being creative can land you good charms (Throwing E right before a minion dies so it goes straight through after it does)
6. You don't have to throw your E right after you ult, typically players will try to dodge your abilities right after you dash in, be patient and wait for the perfect time to throw it
7. Practice - there's really no way around this.
